{{Short description|Type of game}}
'''Games of mental skill''' are [[games of skill]] in which success depends primarily on [[intellectual ability]] rather than [[physical effort]]. They usually involve [[strategy]], [[logic]], [[memory]], [[concentration]], [[planning]], [[calculation]], [[pattern recognition]], or [[problem solving]]. 

Games of mental skill can be played individually or competitively and may include [[board games]], [[card games]], [[abstract strategy games]], [[Puzzle|puzzle games]], [[memory competitions]], [[word games]], and other forms of structured [[mental activity]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Intellectual Games |url=https://changingminds.org/disciplines/game_design/types_game/games_intellectual.htm |publisher=Changing Minds |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Definition of mind sport |url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/mind-sport |publisher=Collins English Dictionary |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

==Overview==
The term is broader than [[mind sport]], which generally refers to organized competitive activities with formal governing bodies, rankings, and championships. While all mind sports are games of mental skill, not all games of mental skill are considered mind sports. For example, [[crossword puzzles]], [[Sudoku]], [[escape-room puzzles]], [[trivia games]], and many [[educational games]] may require considerable intellectual ability without being recognized as formal sports.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kobiela |first=Filip |title=Should chess and other mind sports be regarded as sports? |journal=Journal of the Philosophy of Sport |volume=45 |issue=3 |year=2018 |pages=279–295 |doi=10.1080/00948705.2018.1520125}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mind Sports |url=https://www.topendsports.com/sport/mind-sports.htm |publisher=Topend Sports |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

Games of mental skill may involve complete information, as in [[chess]] or [[go (game)|go]], or hidden information, as in [[poker]] and [[contract bridge]]. Some games emphasize long-term strategy, while others rely more on memory, deduction, or quick thinking. Competitive forms often develop formal rules, rating systems, and organized tournaments over time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mind Sports: Exploring Motivation and Use of Cognitive Strategies in Bridge |url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10049287/ |publisher=PubMed Central |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mind Sports |url=https://www.topendsports.com/sport/mind-sports.htm |publisher=Topend Sports |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

Common examples of games of mental skill include [[chess]], [[draughts]], [[go (game)|go]], [[contract bridge]], [[poker]], [[shogi]], [[xiangqi]], [[mahjong]], ''[[Scrabble]]'', [[Sudoku]], [[crossword puzzles]], [[Rubik's Cube solving]], [[memory competitions]], and various logic-based [[video games]]. Some of these activities have international federations and world championships, while others remain informal recreational activities.<ref>{{cite web |title=About IMSA |url=https://imsa.sport/about/ |publisher=International Mind Sports Association |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mind Sports |url=https://www.topendsports.com/sport/mind-sports.htm |publisher=Topend Sports |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>
